conclusions: Ten longer attempts per standalone mode complete 100000 iterations and 1500000 checks each. No failures appear unmodified, under unpatched LLDB, or with the post-store guard. These samples do not isolate an instrumentation effect.

A separate arm64 C/assembly executable performs 100 million selections per run across FCSEL versus branch and none/yield/sleep schedules; all six runs pass. This is a relocated, synthetic sequence, not proof of correct execution at the engine site or a complete hardware test.

The unchanged staged static browser case fails 2/10, at attempts 6 and 8, iterations 8481 and 781, slot 4. Staged/source values reread 2048, consumed array slot is +0, lower-bound rejection is correct for that zero. Both failures occur immediately after a timer yield.

Every browser attempt verifies the same efb634fa1e5a8e080e27d177aefcaf181534675c900e60f7649bead66fc5efb9 probe hash and requests only / and /probe.js. Browser startup observations remain JIT-disabled.

Read-only LLInt disassembly shows the numeric fast path for op_lesseq decodes with explicit branches and FMOV/SCVTF then FCMP/CSET, without FCSEL. Its numeric slow path does use FCSEL. This does not identify which path or tier executed the original editor false comparison.
No native array-conversion fault has been captured, no production fix is validated, and the array-zero and original false-comparison symptoms are not proven to share a cause.
